author: Leadership Now Project
title: Leadership Now Project Applauds Passage of 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, Urges President Trump to Sign the Bill into Law
text:
Leadership Now Project celebrates the bipartisan congressional passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a key step towards addressing the nationwide affordability crisis affecting millions of families. This sweeping legislation includes critical provisions to cut red tape, expand the housing supply, and make it easier for more Americans to afford a home.
The bill’s fate is now uncertain, as President Trump has announced he will withhold his signature until Congress passes the SAVE America Act to restrict voting access. Common sense, bipartisan legislation should never be held hostage; we urge the president to sign the bill immediately.
“The bipartisan support for the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act highlights the growing consensus that the country needs a new approach to housing policy,” said Leadership Now Project CEO Daniella Ballou-Aares. “Leadership Now has long advocated for elected officials to address the country’s chronic housing shortage by increasing supply and lowering costs for families. We look forward to continuing our work on this issue with state and federal partners, who will be aided by this legislation in their efforts to bring down exorbitant housing costs for Americans.”
In May, Leadership Now launched its Business Plan for America , a policy agenda to strengthen U.S. competitiveness, broaden economic prosperity, and build effective and trusted governing institutions. The Business Plan identifies access to housing as central to our shared economic future and outlines solutions for Congress to boost housing supply and affordability.
“The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act takes aim at several of the biggest obstacles to building more housing in America,” said Bryan Sanchez, housing policy advisor to Leadership Now’s Business Plan for America. “Streamlining permitting, incentivizing pro-housing land use reforms, and making it easier to build manufactured housing are key steps to tackling this challenge. While these are important first steps, more work still needs to be done to address the full scale of America’s housing shortage.”
At this critical moment for the future of U.S. housing, Leadership Now urges President Trump to sign this bill into law and begin providing relief for communities across the country. For more information on the Leadership Now Project’s position on housing, please refer to our policy paper, “ More Homes, Lower Costs .”
